newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 1996 vehicle production hits record high.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 1996 vehicle production hits record high.

text.p: Total production of motor vehicles in Mexico rose 30.1 percent in 1996 to a record 1,211,297 units from 931,178 the year before, the Mexican Association of Automobile Industries said in a statement.
The Association said that total sales rose 35.5 percent in 1996 to 1,309,300, or 343,281 more than in 1995.
In 1996 there were 975,368 vehicles exported from Mexico, or 24.9 percent more than the 781,082 exported in 1995, it said.
The 1996 production was the highest level since 1994, when the previous record was reached at 1,097,381.
Production for the internal market in 1996 rose 57.7 percent compared with the year before to reach a total of 240,423, it said.
But production for the internal market was still down 54 percent compared with the 1994 level.
Wholesale sales in the internal market rose 80.6 percent to 333,932 in 1996 compared with the 184,937 in 1995, it said.
Internal retail sales in 1996 were 43.6 percent higher at 325,087 in 1996 from the year before, but still down 44.9 percent from the 1994 level.
The Association said it was obvious the trend seen in 1995 was changing direction, "however, the success was not enough to push the internal market higher than half of the level reached in 1994."
